statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of eight representative public paths. Not covered: every one of roughly 200 calculators, authenticated account states, account creation/recovery completion, ad click-throughs, and real payment/subscription flows; sampled pages represent the shared homepage, listing, calculator/article, account, locale-data and HTTP-error templates.

page.notes: Server-rendered calculator/reference MPA with shared CSS, inline handlers, a web manifest and Google advertising. Core content is available without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: dark screenshot + computed media/CSS probe on home and calculator
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture (both 77,004-byte PNGs), and the DOM CSS fixes body and panels to white without color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rules.

checkOutcomes.method: reduced-motion animation probe across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: Reduced-motion probe matched reduce=true and found zero active animations or autoplay; there is no non-essential motion to suppress.
Forced-colors screenshot kept text, controls, focus rings and chart labels visible at 360px.
DOM/CSS inspection across the MPA templates found no @view-transition rule, view-transition-name, or pageswap/pagereveal handling.
DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-linked animation or custom scroll event animation to move onto the main thread.
Representative templates use native scrolling and ordinary links/forms; no custom pointermove/swipe implementation fights platform gestures.
No sticky or affixed chrome exists on sampled templates, so there is no scroll-state UI that can become stale.
Computed CSS defines #tt with position:absolute, while calculator help icons use custom click handlers; no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try rules were found.
Breadcrumbs identify hierarchy, active category navigation is highlighted, and calculator results appear directly after the form with a contrasting Result heading.
All load screenshots show core content immediately with no modal, consent wall or full-screen interstitial.

The homepage calculator and Search use span[onclick], and the BMI save action is an img[onclick]. The probe counted two non-native click targets on BMI; these controls are absent from normal keyboard semantics.
At 360px, the calculator and result dominate the first viewport; header is 60px and navigation/sidebar chrome collapses.
Layout evidence on home, mortgage and BMI reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and horizontalOverflowPx=0.
CSS inspection found no @container/container-type usage; calculator, result and navigation components are sized with fixed widths and global max-width media queries.
The BMI probe listed numerous 15-22px-high links; Lighthouse failed target-size for adjacent 17px chart links. Homepage calculator spans and Search are not keyboard controls.
Each sampled entry/detail page has a descriptive H1 and the calculator form plus Calculate action in the first viewport.
Mortgage and BMI pages render default end-to-end calculations and results on load; changing values and calculating is a direct single-form flow.
Results are visibly labelled, Clear is available, validation gives a concrete message, and the tested 404 offers search and calculator links.
Lighthouse scored performance 1.00 on home and BMI; BMI LCP 1.17s, TBT 0ms, CLS 0. Trace LCP was 0.92s with no long tasks.
Three layout captures reported CLS 0; all four BMI images have explicit dimensions.
Trace recorded zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 0ms.
Trace LCP was 916ms; the only stylesheet is the expected head CSS, and both candidate scripts were confirmed async.
HAR recorded 327,468 transferred bytes; 252,043 were script and 294,880 (90%) were third-party. Google Publisher Tag implementation alone transferred 201,092 bytes.
axe reported critical label failures: four nodes on BMI (age, height, weight and search) and one on home. The visible table-cell text is not associated with the inputs.
axe found five contrast failures. Lighthouse measured 3.54:1 for cm/kg text and 2.29:1 for the Clear button, below 4.5:1.
axe found no main landmark and 60 BMI regions outside landmarks. Lighthouse also failed heading-order and found data tables whose header cells are td rather than th.
Mobile screenshots show 16px body text, clear headings and readable line wrapping without clipping.
Layout at 360px had zero horizontal overflow on home, mortgage and BMI, but Lighthouse failed target-size and the probe found many controls below 24px high.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.00 on home and BMI and reported no console-error failure.
The image audit found the clickable Save SVG without alt text. DOM inspection shows layout tables, font elements and table cells used as headings; Lighthouse separately failed td-has-header.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.00; probes found no load-time permission request and no paste-prevention behavior.
DOM evidence shows <meta name="description" content=""> on /my-account/sign-in.php, while the other sampled pages have descriptive titles and descriptions.
Raw HTML contains real href links and viewport metadata; robots.txt allows crawling and points to the sitemap.
Sampled public pages returned 200, robots.txt is permissive, sitemap.xml is available, and no accidental noindex was found; no localized duplicate set requires hreflang.
The BMI probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks. Breadcrumb microdata exists, but no metadata describes the calculator/result content for rich sharing.

Headers evidence found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. PHPSESSID and recentVisit were set without Secure and with SameSite=None; PHPSESSID was also not HttpOnly.
Tracker evidence found seven third-party origins and three known tracker domains. HAR attributed 15 of 21 requests and 294,880 of 327,468 transferred bytes to third parties.
The sign-in probe found no WebAuthn/passkey code. Email/password fields have no autocomplete tokens; password is the only first-party sign-in method besides Google OAuth.
The main response lacks clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS and CSP frame-ancestors.
Discoverability reported 100% raw-HTML content coverage on home and mortgage, with title, H1 and description present without JavaScript.
Native page navigation and server-rendered state avoid shell flicker; sampled forms and help content remained within the mobile viewport.

A manifest exists with display:standalone, but has no start_url and only one 192px icon; navigator.serviceWorker.controller was false. Core calculator use therefore has no demonstrated offline fallback.
The tested unknown route returns a real HTTP 404 with a clear explanation, search and links back to calculator categories.
The site declares lang=en, but CSS inspection shows extensive left/right floats, margins, padding and absolute left positioning and no dir attribute or logical-property strategy.

The Date Calculator exposes hidden values such as 07/18/2026 and separate month/day/year controls, with no Intl usage. Currency output renders fixed decimal strings and a hard-coded English date such as Jul. 18, 2026.
The sampled date/currency tools operate on calendar dates and current rates, not cross-zone instants, recurring events or DST-sensitive schedules.
checkOutcomes.reason: The sampled date/currency tools operate on calendar dates and current rates, not cross-zone instants, recurring events or DST-sensitive schedules.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No consent wall, disguised ad, confirmshaming or forced continuity appeared in sampled public flows; account persistence is visible and user-toggleable.
Entering age 0 creates “positive numbers only”, but the input gets no aria-invalid or aria-describedby and the message has no role=alert/status.
The sign-in probe shows empty autocomplete values for email and password, and the email input is type=text rather than type=email.
“stay signed in” is checked by default, the PHP session cookie lacks Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite protection, and no passkey support was found.
The BMI image audit found a below-fold PNG without loading=lazy or srcset; three content images lack responsive source selection.
The core page is fast and small, yet ad and traffic-quality scripts initiate 15 third-party requests and transfer 294,880 bytes, including background configuration requests.
HAR measured 294,880 third-party bytes out of 327,468 total; the 201KB ad implementation is over six times the first-party document transfer.
No WebMCP/agent tool registration was found, and Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored BMI 0.5 because its accessibility tree is malformed by unlabeled fields.
Deterministic calculators do not benefit from probabilistic language-model or summarisation inference.
checkOutcomes.reason: Deterministic calculators do not benefit from probabilistic language-model or summarisation inference.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap around repeated calculator operations
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 calculator operation cycles, heap self-size was 1.93MB versus 1.73MB baseline; modest growth was mostly compiled code/native state, not evidence of unbounded retained interaction objects.
Heap summaries show a small 1.7-1.9MB self-size footprint and roughly 37-39k nodes, proportionate to the page and ad runtime.
Neither heap summary surfaced Detached* constructors; closures rose only 73 across separately loaded sessions and no repeating timer-driven UI was observed.

paths.description: Homepage and embedded scientific calculator; entry, discovery and primary quick-calculation surface.
Financial calculator index; representative listing/navigation template.
Mortgage Calculator; representative finance form, result and long-form explanatory template.
BMI Calculator; representative health form, validation, chart, data table and article template.
Sign-in page; representative account and authentication flow.
Unknown URL; representative HTTP error and recovery state.
Date Calculator; locale-sensitive date input and formatting archetype.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded to a light palette.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture (both 77,004-byte PNGs), and the DOM CSS fixes body and panels to white without color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven surface, text, form and chart colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across the MPA templates found no @view-transition rule, view-transition-name, or pageswap/pagereveal handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressively enhanced @view-transition navigation transition and disable it under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Calculator help tooltips use manual absolute positioning.
findings.evidence: Computed CSS defines #tt with position:absolute, while calculator help icons use custom click handlers; no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a popover anchored with CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks, retaining a conventional fallback.

findings.summary: Core controls are non-semantic click targets.
findings.evidence: The homepage calculator and Search use span[onclick], and the BMI save action is an img[onclick]. The probe counted two non-native click targets on BMI; these controls are absent from normal keyboard semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace clickable spans/images with button elements and give each control an accessible name and visible focus state.

findings.summary: Shared components adapt only through viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container/container-type usage; calculator, result and navigation components are sized with fixed widths and global max-width media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce containment and component-level size queries for reusable calculator/result/navigation modules while preserving viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for touch and some have no keyboard path.
findings.evidence: The BMI probe listed numerous 15-22px-high links; Lighthouse failed target-size for adjacent 17px chart links. Homepage calculator spans and Search are not keyboard controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic buttons/links, provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets with spacing (prefer 44px for primary touch controls), and retain visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Advertising code dominates an otherwise light page.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 327,468 transferred bytes; 252,043 were script and 294,880 (90%) were third-party. Google Publisher Tag implementation alone transferred 201,092 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay ad code until after core content, consent and/or proximity to the ad slot; reduce third-party tags and measure their user value.

findings.summary: Calculator and search inputs lack programmatic labels.
findings.evidence: axe reported critical label failures: four nodes on BMI (age, height, weight and search) and one on home. The visible table-cell text is not associated with the inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate every visible label with its control using label[for]/id; name icon-only save/search controls and use semantic buttons.

findings.summary: Several essential labels and controls fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: axe found five contrast failures. Lighthouse measured 3.54:1 for cm/kg text and 2.29:1 for the Clear button, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text and the Clear control background, then verify all states at WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: Page structure lacks landmarks and uses invalid heading/table semantics.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and 60 BMI regions outside landmarks. Lighthouse also failed heading-order and found data tables whose header cells are td rather than th.
findings.suggestedFix: Add header/main/nav/footer landmarks, make headings sequential, and use caption/th/scope for data tables.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow works, but target sizing does not.
findings.evidence: Layout at 360px had zero horizontal overflow on home, mortgage and BMI, but Lighthouse failed target-size and the probe found many controls below 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the successful fluid reflow and enlarge/space interactive targets without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Some authored HTML and image semantics are unsound.
findings.evidence: The image audit found the clickable Save SVG without alt text. DOM inspection shows layout tables, font elements and table cells used as headings; Lighthouse separately failed td-has-header.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic HTML for layout and tables, and replace the clickable image with a named button containing a decorative SVG.

findings.summary: The public sign-in page has an empty meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows <meta name="description" content=""> on /my-account/sign-in.php, while the other sampled pages have descriptive titles and descriptions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique sign-in description or deliberately noindex the utility page if it should not appear in search.

findings.summary: Calculator detail pages omit social preview metadata and entity-level structured data.
findings.evidence: The BMI probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks. Breadcrumb microdata exists, but no metadata describes the calculator/result content for rich sharing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and appropriate JSON-LD for the visible calculator/software content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline security headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. PHPSESSID and recentVisit were set without Secure and with SameSite=None; PHPSESSID was also not HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark session cookies Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax/Strict as appropriate.

findings.summary: Calculator pages load a large advertising/tracking footprint by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found seven third-party origins and three known tracker domains. HAR attributed 15 of 21 requests and 294,880 of 327,468 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise ad/analytics vendors, gate non-essential requests on informed choice, shorten retention, and batch the remaining analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and omits autofill/passkey support.
findings.evidence: The sign-in probe found no WebAuthn/passkey code. Email/password fields have no autocomplete tokens; password is the only first-party sign-in method besides Google OAuth.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=username/current-password immediately, then offer passkey registration and authentication as a phishing-resistant option.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS and CSP frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy restrictive frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy with CSP reporting, and evaluate Trusted Types for account surfaces.

findings.summary: The calculator app advertises standalone display but has no offline runtime.
findings.evidence: A manifest exists with display:standalone, but has no start_url and only one 192px icon; navigator.serviceWorker.controller was false. Core calculator use therefore has no demonstrated offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Complete the manifest and add a small service worker that caches the shell and provides an explicit offline fallback for calculators that can run locally.

findings.summary: Worldwide content is built with physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: The site declares lang=en, but CSS inspection shows extensive left/right floats, margins, padding and absolute left positioning and no dir attribute or logical-property strategy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dir-aware markup and migrate layout-critical physical properties to inline/block logical properties; test an RTL locale.

findings.summary: Locale-sensitive calculators hard-code US-style dates and number presentation.
findings.evidence: The Date Calculator exposes hidden values such as 07/18/2026 and separate month/day/year controls, with no Intl usage. Currency output renders fixed decimal strings and a hard-coded English date such as Jul. 18, 2026.
findings.suggestedFix: Parse/store unambiguous values and format dates, numbers and currencies with Intl for the selected locale; make locale assumptions explicit.

findings.summary: Validation errors are immediate but not programmatically announced or associated.
findings.evidence: Entering age 0 creates “positive numbers only”, but the input gets no aria-invalid or aria-describedby and the message has no role=alert/status.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, set aria-invalid, connect persistent help/error text with aria-describedby, and announce submit-time summaries.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: The sign-in probe shows empty autocomplete values for email and password, and the email input is type=text rather than type=email.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; add appropriate tokens to account creation forms.

findings.summary: The account entry flow defaults to persistent sign-in without modern account protections.
findings.evidence: “stay signed in” is checked by default, the PHP session cookie lacks Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite protection, and no passkey support was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a safer session-cookie posture, explain persistence, reconsider the checked default on shared devices, and add passkey/account-session management.

findings.summary: Below-fold imagery is not responsively delivered or deferred.
findings.evidence: The BMI image audit found a below-fold PNG without loading=lazy or srcset; three content images lack responsive source selection.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images and provide responsive AVIF/WebP sources where raster content benefits.

findings.summary: Background advertising work is disproportionate to the core calculator.
findings.evidence: The core page is fast and small, yet ad and traffic-quality scripts initiate 15 third-party requests and transfer 294,880 bytes, including background configuration requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer background fetches until idle/consent/visibility, remove redundant traffic-quality work, and enforce a third-party budget.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes about 90% of transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 294,880 third-party bytes out of 327,468 total; the 201KB ad implementation is over six times the first-party document transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and monitor a third-party byte/request budget; lazy-load ads and remove vendors that do not justify their resource and privacy cost.

findings.summary: High-value calculator actions are difficult for agents to invoke safely.
findings.evidence: No WebMCP/agent tool registration was found, and Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored BMI 0.5 because its accessibility tree is malformed by unlabeled fields.
findings.suggestedFix: First fix form semantics, then consider exposing selected calculators as typed, constrained WebMCP tools with clear inputs and deterministic outputs.

taskList.title: Make forms and custom controls semantic, labelled, keyboard/touch accessible
Deploy security headers and secure session-cookie defaults
Reduce and consent-gate the ad/tracker footprint
Improve sign-in autofill and add passkeys
Add progressive cross-document transitions and modern tooltip anchoring
Expose selected calculators as safe structured agent tools
